text: Introduction to Search Engine Optimization. Making Websites Discoverable on Google. SEO (Search Engine Optimization) is the process of improving organic visibility. Search engine crawlers (Googlebot) read and index HTML structure. Well-structured HTML ranks higher and drives free organic user traffic. On-page technical SEO begins with clean semantic HTML tags and metadata.

The Crucial <title> Element. Your Webpage's Most Critical Meta Tag. The <title> tag appears as the clickable blue headline in search results. Appears in the browser tab and when sharing links on social platforms. Best Practice: Keep titles between 50 and 60 characters for full display. Include the primary keyword near the beginning of the title string.

The <meta name="description"> Tag. The Search Result Snippet Description. Provides a concise summary of page content below the title headline. Influences Click-Through Rate (CTR) directly from the search results page. Best Practice: Keep meta descriptions between 140 and 160 characters. Include a compelling call-to-action (e.g., 'Learn HTML free today').

Responsive Viewport Configuration. Mobile-First Indexing and Viewport Scaling. Google uses mobile-first indexing: mobile pages determine ranking. The viewport meta tag ensures pages scale correctly on mobile devices. width=device-width sets width to match the screen's physical pixels. initial-scale=1.0 sets the initial zoom level when first loaded.

Semantic HTML for Search Engines. Meaningful Elements vs Generic <div> Tags. Semantic elements describe their meaning to both browser and developer. Use <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <section>, and <footer>. Replaces meaningless generic <div> soup with clear content boundaries. Helps search engines identify primary content from navigation boilerplate.

Image SEO & Alt Text Optimization. Ranking in Google Images and Image Accessibility. Search engines cannot directly 'see' images; they read the alt attribute. Write clear, descriptive alt text explaining image contents accurately. Include relevant keywords naturally without spamming keyword lists. Use modern compressed formats like WebP or AVIF for fast image loading.

Introduction to Core Web Vitals. Google's Official User Experience Ranking Signals. Core Web Vitals are official Google ranking signals measuring page speed. Focuses on three real-world metrics: Loading, Interactivity, and Stability. LCP measures perceived loading speed of the largest visual element. INP measures how quickly the page responds to user clicks and taps. CLS measures visual layout stability and prevents unexpected shifts.

Largest Contentful Paint (LCP). Measuring Loading Performance for Main Content. LCP marks the point when the page's main content has likely loaded. Measures the render time of the largest image or text block in viewport. Target Threshold: Under 2.5 seconds is rated 'Good' by Google. Fixes: Compress hero images, use CDN hosting, and remove render-blocking CSS.

Interaction to Next Paint (INP). Measuring Responsiveness to User Input. INP replaced First Input Delay (FID) as the official responsiveness metric. Measures the latency of all user interactions (clicks, taps, typing). Target Threshold: Under 200 milliseconds is rated 'Good'. Fixes: Break up long JavaScript tasks and avoid blocking the main thread.

Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Ensuring Visual Stability During Page Load. CLS measures unexpected layout shifts of visible elements as resources load. Prevents frustrating misclicks when buttons move while you tap them. Target Threshold: Score under 0.1 is rated 'Good'. Fixes: Always declare width and height on images, videos, and ads.

Auditing with Google Chrome Lighthouse. Comprehensive Automated Quality Inspection. Lighthouse is an automated auditing tool built into Chrome DevTools. Evaluates Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO scores (0–100). Identifies unoptimized images, unused CSS, and missing meta tags. Provides specific, actionable recommendations for optimization.

Practical Optimization Techniques. High-Impact Performance Improvements. 1. Modern Formats: Convert JPEG/PNG to modern WebP or AVIF formats. 2. Lazy Loading: Add loading="lazy" to off-screen images and iframes. 3. Script Loading: Use defer or async on external script tags. 4. Asset Minification: Minify CSS and JavaScript to reduce byte size.

Common SEO Misconceptions. Separating Outdated Myths from Effective Strategies. Myth 1: 'Keyword stuffing increases rankings' — Google penalizes spam. Myth 2: 'Meta keywords tag matters' — Ignored by Google since 2009. Truth 1: Focus on user search intent, clear answers, and fast page load. Truth 2: High-quality, original educational content always wins over hacks.

Lecture 3 Summary & Course Wrap-up. Recap of SEO, Core Web Vitals & Web Fundamentals. Technical SEO begins with accurate <title>, meta description, and semantics. Core Web Vitals are Google ranking signals: LCP (speed), INP, and CLS. Audit your projects regularly using Chrome Lighthouse. You now understand HTML structure, media embedding, and web optimization!
